Late Summer Heatwave Hits Greece Hard – Temperatures to Exceed 100F for a Week in Several Areas
ATHENS – Greece is in the grip of a heatwave, with temperatures locally expected to exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit. Essentially, this is the first heatwave of the summer, and it will be a prolonged one,” Kostas Lagouvardos, Research Director at the National Observatory of Athens and head of the METEO/NOA unit, told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (ANA-MPA) on August. He added that the areas expected to record the highest temperatures are Thessaly, Western Greece, and Central Macedonia.
According to the latest data, the most difficult days will be Saturday August 22, and Sunday the 23rd, while heatwave conditions will prevail in many areas until the middle of next week.
It’s a peculiar late-onset heatwave. According to METEO/NOA, air masses over Greece will be 6 to 8 ° C warmer than normal for this time of year.
Lagouvardos stressed that this is not an extreme heatwave in terms of the intensity of the temperatures. However, the high temperatures are expected to persist for six to seven days, while the projected end of the heatwave will be reassessed at the beginning of next week based on the latest forecast data.
“The weekend will be the hottest period. Temperatures will fall in the eastern and southern parts of the country on Monday and Tuesday, but this will not be the case elsewhere. In Western Greece, Central Macedonia and Thessaly, high temperatures will continue. From Monday onwards, the meltemia winds will also strengthen, which will help areas such as Attiki, the Cyclades, and northern Crete. Winds will reach up to Force 5, locally reaching Force 6 to 7 in the south and south-east,” Lagouvardos told ANA-MPA.
He also noted that the risk of wildfires will be elevated, as the high temperatures will contribute to further drying out of the available fuel.
“Therefore, the fire-weather indices are deteriorating day by day, particularly as the winds will strengthen considerably from Monday onwards,” he said, stressing that temperatures of this magnitude are unusual towards the end of August.
Material from ANA-MPA was used in this report.
